clue.text: Taken in to cut tails off fish

parts.note: to be taken in is to be had, fooled
to dock an animal is to cut its tail short

explanation.surface: Someone deceived into trimming the tails off fish at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family, a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: Uncomfortable bed — hence boxer's complaint

parts.note: a hard seat or bed is uncomfortable
pad is slang for a bed or place to sleep

explanation.surface: A fighter grumbling about a lumpy bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not a fighter; HARDPAD is a form of canine distemper that hardens the paw pads.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardpad is a viral illness of dogs, so it is an ailment a boxer dog could suffer from.

clue.text: A different way to produce entertainment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an alternative route when a road is closed
second meaning: an amusement or pastime

explanation.surface: A novel method of putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a detour around a road closure and also a pleasant distraction or amusement.

clue.text: Award just over 50 critical marks on paper

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An exam marker giving just over half marks.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped symbols used by scholars to flag doubtful passages in manuscripts, so editorial annotations.

clue.text: Gentle handlers juvenile gets, initially, and appreciates

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning of the preceding word, keeping only its first letter

parts.note: first letter of this word
to love something is to appreciate it

explanation.surface: A young person who appreciates being treated gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone with kid gloves means dealing delicately with them, so the phrase names the instruments of soft handling.

clue.text: Game to play in naval base

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game
to sport is to play or frolic

explanation.surface: Sailors playing a game while stationed at their base.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSPORT is a town on Portsmouth Harbour in Hampshire, long home to Royal Navy establishments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hampshire town across the harbour from Portsmouth has hosted Royal Navy submarine and training establishments for centuries.

clue.text: Ostentatious feast

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an annual college dinner for old members

explanation.walkthrough: A gaudy is a reunion dinner at Oxford colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tastelessly showy, and the noun is a celebratory university banquet for alumni.

clue.text: Only one part of this clue has two of these

definitions.text: Only one part of this clue has two of these

parts.words: Only one part of this clue has two of these
parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle about some component of the sentence

parts.words: Only one part of this clue has two of these
parts.note: setter's reading: every word of the clue is monosyllabic except the first, which has two sound units

explanation.walkthrough: Count the beats: 'On-ly' is the one word with two; every other word in the clue has one.
explanation.definitionFit: The units of pronunciation into which words divide are the thing counted, and only the opening word has two.

clue.text: House call charge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Speaker's cry for quiet in the House of Commons
second meaning: a command or instruction

explanation.surface: A doctor's home visit and its fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House call' looks like a doctor's visit, but it is the Speaker of the House of Commons shouting for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commons Speaker calls the chamber to silence with this word, and as a noun it also means an instruction given.

clue.text: Political leader in tribute that's rigged at the highest level

definitions.text: that's rigged at the highest level

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the leader goes inside the tribute word

parts.note: a toast is a drink in tribute to someone
PM, Prime Minister, leads a government

explanation.surface: A prime minister honoured with a tribute that's been fixed by top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigged' looks like corrupted, as in a fixed vote, but it is a ship's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the mast section above the lower mast on a sailing ship, fitted with rigging high up.

clue.text: Said to comment critically on entertainment

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the next phrase rather than one spelt like it

parts.note: to review a show is to comment critically on it

explanation.surface: Someone reported to have panned a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The critic's verb REVIEW is pronounced exactly like the French-derived stage word.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical show of sketches, songs and dances, a form of stage amusement.

clue.text: Showing effect of suffering in crowded accommodation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bent over in pain
second meaning: sharing a room or bed with another

explanation.surface: Someone visibly in distress from being crammed into overcrowded lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a body bent forward in agony and also two people sharing space meant for one.

clue.text: Celebration including one and all, to some extent

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the celebration word wraps around the others

parts.note: a party is a celebration
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party where everyone joins in, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One and all' reads as everyone, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Partially means in part or not completely, which is exactly to a limited degree.

clue.text: A judicial process prematurely concluded in courts

indicators.note: something concluded prematurely stops before its natural end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a trial is a judicial process

explanation.surface: A legal case abandoned early in the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' looks like the law courts of the surface, but it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards or halls in buildings, plural of atrium, a sense of court as an enclosed space.

clue.text: Daughter's fault, this state of indecision

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a rift is a fault or crack, as in a geological fault

explanation.surface: A parent blaming a daughter for family uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift means aimless inaction, letting things slide without deciding on any purposeful course.

clue.text: Revolutionary form of punishment

parts.note: surface reading: a penalty imposed by rebels or a radical new sentence
setter's reading: a penal device that literally goes round, worked by prisoners stepping on it

explanation.walkthrough: Victorian prisoners were set to tread a large wheel for hours as hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating stepped wheel was a nineteenth-century prison punishment, and it turns round and round.

clue.text: Evil edict rewritten in other words

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again differently, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked decree reworded so that it means something else.
explanation.walkthrough: VIDELICET is the Latin word abbreviated as viz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term, meaning namely or that is to say, introduces a restatement or clarification.

clue.text: Import from France demanded by customs

definitions.text: Import from France demanded by customs

parts.words: Import from France demanded by customs
parts.note: surface reading: French goods that border officials insist on inspecting

parts.words: Import from France demanded by customs
parts.note: setter's reading: a phrase borrowed from French meaning required by social convention

explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' looks like the border service, but it means social conventions; the answer is a French phrase taken into English.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French expression means required by etiquette or fashion, strictly obligatory according to accepted social practice.

clue.text: What makes Conservative viewer endlessly mad? Lots of offensive behaviour

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the following word goes
asking what the pieces make invites building a new word out of their letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A question about what enrages a Tory television watcher, answered with a rise in bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the anger of the surface, but it only supplies letters; the anagram signal is 'What makes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime wave is a sudden surge in the number of offences committed, a spate of lawbreaking.

clue.text: In one role, father forces son to change

indicators.note: to change means to be altered, so these letters must be reorganised

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dad pressuring his boy to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a parent, but it is a priest, who in one of his roles hears confessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic priest who hears penitents' sins in the sacrament of penance is called a confessor.

clue.text: Trapped in wretched darkness? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: something trapped in is held inside, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone caught in miserable darkness, told 'Hard luck!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang for hard luck, but here it is literal: Cheddar is a hard cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a firm English cheese from Somerset, an example of a hard variety.

clue.text: Silent picture

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a single photograph taken from a film

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a silent movie; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hushed and motionless, and as a noun names a single photographic frame from a movie.

clue.text: Gallery redesigned to a considerable extent

indicators.note: redesigned means laid out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An art gallery heavily remodelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely means mostly or mainly, for the greater part, which is to a great degree.

clue.text: After opening letter, stopped and relaxed

indicators.note: taking only what comes after the opening letter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Someone who, after opening a letter, stopped and calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or slackened, made less tense, which is a close synonym of relaxed.

clue.text: Comment derisively on rations

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at the food handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff as a noun is British slang for food or grub.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock contemptuously, and as informal slang the noun means grub or provisions.

clue.text: Sabbatical leave? There's a long way to go

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a year that is light on work
second meaning: the astronomical unit of distance light travels in a year

explanation.surface: An academic's year off sounds like a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful: a sabbatical is a light year of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomical unit is the vast distance light covers in twelve months, while the pun reads a work-free year as easy.

clue.text: Some instruments, or others, less loud at first

indicators.note: less means minus, so the musical abbreviation for loud is taken away from the front

parts.note: other instruments, wind ones
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A musical note about instruments that should play quieter at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F from the front of FLUTES, other instruments, to leave plucked ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked stringed instruments with a pear-shaped body, so they are examples of musical instruments.

clue.text: Oriental's capital has to include adequate yen

indicators.note: include means hold within, so the word to wraps around what follows

parts.note: taken as written
OK means adequate
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An Asian business person's funds must contain enough Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: OK and Y go inside T...O; 'capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the seat of government of Japan, the Far Eastern nation's principal city.

clue.text: Character led to toil with difficulty

indicators.note: doing something with difficulty suggests struggle and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A person driven to hard work despite struggles.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza DOOLITTLE in Pygmalion and Dr DOOLITTLE are both famous fictional characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolittle is a fictional figure: the flower girl of Shaw's Pygmalion or Lofting's animal-talking doctor.

clue.text: Honour amongst thieves

parts.note: surface reading: the proverbial code of loyalty among criminals
setter's reading: an honour card in a pack who is himself a rogue

explanation.walkthrough: In card games the top cards (ace, king, queen, jack, ten) are called honours; the jack's old name also means a dishonest man.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack card is an honour in bridge and whist, and the same old word means a scoundrel or rogue.

clue.text: Fictitious burglar's gambling enterprises

definitions.meaning: first meaning: E. W. Hornung's gentleman thief
second meaning: lotteries with prizes drawn from sold tickets

explanation.surface: A fictional thief who also runs betting schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Raffles is the cricket-playing gentleman cat burglar of Hornung's stories; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornung's character is a famous fictional housebreaker, and lotteries for prizes are a form of betting operation.

clue.text: Seals king inside castle yard

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular answer: the place where seals breed

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the king goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: the rook is the castle in chess
ER, Edwardus Rex, is a king's cipher
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A king who keeps seals in his castle courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' looks like a verb, a king sealing documents, but it is the animals. ER, Edwardus Rex, is a king's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a breeding colony, used for seals and penguins as well as for rooks.
